meaning: A lossless, source-bound verification input projection joins one registered compiled graph to one registered reconciled compilation plan without claiming that required verification has run.
preconditions: Require the original unchanged registered graph, current graph obligations, and registered reconciled plan whose complete compiled certificate matches that graph. Detached plans, JSON graph clones, mutated graphs and cross-project or stale graph-plan joins reject without filesystem reads or writes.
preservation: Preserve the complete root-independent compiled semantic graph, including all typed bodies, field constructors, qualified relationships, applicability, witnesses and outcomes. Preserve the authored compilation selection, generator requests, selected definition bytes, native module ownership/import/export inventory, exact artifact inventory and each qualified node view. Only the local source-root location is excluded as relocation metadata.
finite_certificate: Use the existing compiler-refinement certificate over the full node and edge projection. This binds finite source/graph identity and obligation denominators; it does not prove generated behavior, native compilation or Lean checking. Do not lower new typed contracts into the incompatible legacy formalization shape.
requirements: Carry all existing shared artifact-plan verification obligations unchanged, plus source currentness, compiled graph obligations, source-and-selection preservation, isolated exact-source replay, successor formalization currentness and exact output currentness. Requirements have no success status and cannot be waived by serialization, registration, hashing or a successful input validation.
identity: The projection digest binds the exact definition, source identities, compiled and finite-projection certificates, checked plan/capsule identities, complete projected meaning, native inventory and evidence requirements. Deterministic identical sources and selections agree across roots; changes to meaning or selected bindings remain visible in payload fields, not only hashes.
validation: Validate inert projected data against a fresh reconstruction from the supplied checked graph and plan, including exact keys, arrays, requirement coverage and claim ceiling. Recomputed caller digests are insufficient. Return a newly registered immutable projection; rendering requires registration and emits canonical JSON only.
scope: Verification input projection only. No native compiler, semantic observer, formalizer, proof kernel, provider, source authoring or output publisher is executed. Existing verify-project rejection and legacy formalization guards remain until successor verification and formalization actually satisfy their requirements.
